facades._: Facade colours MEASURED from 4K walk (Nov 2023, eye level) and drone (Nov 2022, overcast) footage, 2026-08-03 — see git history. walls = the dominant wall tone; accents = the secondary materials on the same building; styles = which facade tile it wears. Every key must name a mass the renderer actually builds (tests/campus-facades.test.mjs pins that) — the previous file spent eleven entries on names the data does not carry, and they drew nothing. WS-E4 (2026-08-06) populated the masses section from campus-eighth.json's Eighth College dossier: Sankofa Tower (m:-68,594, #cdc5c7) reuses the fins tile — its measured 2m vertical-bay/glazed-notch precast rhythm is a narrow-pier-over-recessed-glass read that fins already draws. Podemos (m:-56,528, #d4cbc9) reuses eggcrate — its punched-window-grid on precast is a deep two-axis grid, the same rhythm eggcrate was built for. Sankofa Mid (m:-116,613, #efe7e9) and Azad (m:-182,614, #d8d3d3) are ordinary punched-window stucco with no standout rhythm in the footage, so they keep the default band (no style key) rather than force a tile that oversells the read. Pulse Tower (m:-154,556) and Pulse Mid (m:-186,562), both #e2dade from the same source facade (r1c1-plan-00-south.png), share a new `paired` tile: their measured paired-bay rhythm (windows grouped in twos per structural bay) did not fit any of the eight existing tiles cleanly — band, ribbon and bands assume a continuous run, balcony and glass assume a void or curtain wall, fins and eggcrate assume a single-window grid — so one new tile was added rather than force a mismatch; it is the only new tile this workstream introduces. Sankofa Base (m:-97,609) stays out of masses entirely: the dossier resolved only a canopy accent, never a wall colour (occluded in every captured frame), and an unmeasured wall is better absent than guessed. Cross-check: all 6 masses' campus-arcgis.json massing.levels exactly equal the dossier's visually-counted storeys (21/16/10/9/10/9) with h/levels ≈ 3.05m for every one, so there is no GIS-vs-frame storey disagreement for Eighth. 2026-08-06, later: WS-E4 covered six masses but MISSED Survivance, whose two masses therefore fell through to the name key `Survivance` = #c9ad85, a tan that the Apple 3D capture flatly contradicts — it is the same white as its neighbours. Added m:-156,668 (main mass, 33.5 m / 11 levels) = #efebee, sampled from .cache/eighth-area/r4c2-oblique-00-south.png by splitting the facade rectangle at its own median luminance and taking the median of the light half, so windows and shadow do not drag the wall tone down. The sampler was calibrated on this file's own trusted answers before being believed: it returned #efebed for Sankofa Mid (recorded #efe7e9) and #d2cacc for Sankofa Tower (recorded #cdc5c7). Survivance's 6.1 m base (m:-142,666) stays out for the same reason Sankofa Base does — its dark bronze-grey reads clearly in the frames but was not measured, and an unmeasured wall is better absent than guessed. PROVENANCE CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (independent review, verified by recomputing every station-to-mass distance with the repo own toLocal): the sentence above names r4c2-oblique-00-south.png as the source frame for Survivance #efebee. That citation is NOT defensible. r4c2 is indeed the closest capture station to Survivance, but at 55.5 m, and the nearest mass to r4c2 is AZAD at 23 m with Sankofa Mid second at 43 m — Survivance is only third in its own source frame. Without a recorded camera pose for the Apple captures there is no way to project footprints into the frame and prove which facade the patch covered, so #efebee is a NEIGHBOURHOOD reading, not a per-building measurement. It is kept rather than reverted because the direction is not in doubt — Survivance stands plainly the same near-white as its neighbours in the Apple 3D capture, and the tan #c9ad85 it replaced was contradicted by every frame it appears in — but it must be treated as provisional and re-measured from a station-registered capture. The same caution applies to any hex in campus-eighth.json whose station-proximity justification was recomputed and found false. 2026-08-16, Revelle photo pass: York Hall and Argo Hall each carried a wall colour and no style, so both drew the default band — wrong for the two most-seen facades in Revelle Plaza. York Hall = fins is SOURCED: STRUCTURE magazine's account of LPA's seismic rehabilitation states 805 story-tall precast concrete fins wrap its upper floors (https://www.structuremag.org/article/shipshape-the-seismic-rehabilitation-of-york-hall/, with LPA's own project page https://lpadesignstudios.com/projects/york-hall-ucsd for the 300-foot, 35-column arcade beneath them). Argo Hall = fins is MEASURED off dated Wikimedia photographs (Argo_Hall.jpg, 2012; Revelle_Plaza.jpg, 2006): a dense field of vertical precast blade fins runs the full height of every residential floor in front of a continuous glazed band, at ~1.5-1.6 m centres over a ~3.05 m floor-to-floor. Blake Hall was NOT given a style — it is plainly the same family at four storeys, but no clean photograph of it was found and that is an inference, not a measurement. Urey Hall keeps balcony, which is right on its long side wing even though the plaza-facing corner is two blank board-formed stair towers; the corner is built as photo-sourced detail instead of by retuning the tile.

eighth._: WS-E1 measurement dossier for Eighth College, built 2026-08-06. Every entry keyed by mass hash m:<cx>,<cz> = Math.round(vertex-average centroid) of the docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing ring at build-campus-truecolor.mjs's keyOf() rule (rings /10) — verified against the actual massing polygons, which in one case (Sankofa Base) round 1m differently than the hand-given task centroid, so these keys are the polygon-derived ones, not the hand-rounded ones. Colours sampled with scripts/tmp-sample.mjs (median of a masked pixel patch) from Apple Maps 3D captures ONLY (.cache/apple-flyover, .cache/eighth-area) per the epoch rule — never from .cache/tiles-orbit, which is Google mid-construction imagery used only to cross-check facade geometry. Storey counts are GIS docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing.levels, visually corroborated by counting window rows in a lit frame; bay_m is a VISUAL-ESTIMATE class measurement (piers counted in a near-corner, least-foreshortened crop, scaled by a floor-height calibration derived from the same crop) — treat it as a candidate figure, not survey-grade. Buildings with no captured station within useful range (Survivance tower+low sit toward the uncaptured r3 row) or with a facade never legibly resolved (Podemos low, unnamed dining pavilion, most of Sankofa Base) are OMITTED or marked resolved:false rather than guessed — see the builder report for the full per-mass account. WS-E2 (2026-08-06) added the ground key: 74 ground-plane features for Eighth (1 basketball court, 19 walkway/paving-zone, 7 courtyard, 47 planting-bed), all snapped to already-surveyed docs/data/campus-arcgis.json ground[] polygons (registration arcgis.ground#<index>, ring coords /10 to get metres) rather than hand-measured off Apple pixels, per the tasks own STRONGLY PREFERRED guidance. The basketball court is additionally photo-confirmed (r1c2-plan-00-south.png, blue surface + white key markings) and its surface colour sampled from that frame. courtyard/planting-bed kind is a >200sqm size heuristic (shoelace-formula polygon area, corrected 2026-08-06 cycle-2 from an earlier bounding-box-area computation that had misclassified 10 sub-200sqm polygons as courtyard) over GIS green polygons (GIS does not itself distinguish lawn/courtyard from planting bed) — not individually photo-confirmed per polygon. arcgis.ground#409 (a 9.7sqm sliver on a 21m-long, <0.5m-wide diagonal strip) was dropped rather than mislabeled: its shape is not a real distinct planting/courtyard feature, almost certainly a walkway-edge fragment misrouted into the green layer. Stepped terraces and stair flights were investigated but OMITTED: docs/data/textures ground-texture chunks covering Eighth (chunk_3_8.jpg, chunk_4_8.jpg) are themselves mid-construction-epoch Google imagery (visible scaffolding/bare dirt), so texture-chunk registration is contaminated for this area exactly like .cache/tiles-orbit and cannot be used; a real stair+handrail was located in eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png near a western courtyard, but the flight descends into a photogrammetry mesh reconstruction gap (a jagged dark hole artifact) that makes per-step run/rise unmeasurable to the required confidence, so it was left out rather than guessed (frames tried: r1c2-plan-00-south.png — hard shadow at the Sankofa Base plinth; r1c1-plan-00-south.png — no stair geometry resolved, only a road kerb ramp; r2c1-plan-00-south.png — real stair found but occluded by a mesh gap beyond the top ~5 treads). One oversized arcgis green polygon cluster (#1127, 73.7x184.5m, and #1160, 63.6x46m) was excluded as too large/ambiguous to label a single courtyard-scale feature (likely hillside greenbelt) rather than mislabel it. CORRECTIONS 2026-08-06 (independent review; every figure below recomputed from the manifest with the repo own toLocal and cross-checked against the camera eighth-compare.mjs emits): (1) THREE station-proximity claims in the buildings notes are false by 4-8x and two invert the argument they were written to make. Podemos: stated 7.8 m from r1c3 with the next-nearest Eighth mass 70 m+ away; actual 59.2 m, and Pulse Tower is nearer to r1c3 at 52.2 m. Azad: stated 13.7 m from r2c1 and the closest station-to-mass match in the dossier; actual 65.7 m, and Pulse Mid is nearer at 20.0 m. Sankofa Base: stated 20 m from r2c2; actual 84.4 m. The CONCLUSIONS survive re-derivation on correctly chosen stations — Podemos true nearest station is r1c4 at 16.1 m where Podemos IS the nearest mass, and Azad true nearest is r4c1 at 21.2 m where Azad IS the nearest mass — so no colour is overturned by this, but the stated reasoning was wrong and nothing in the repo would have caught it. (2) The claim that Survivance sits toward an uncaptured r3 row is false: all 25 stations r0c0-r4c4 are on disk, and r3c0 (23:55) and r4c2 (00:44) both predate the WS-E1 commit at 01:10. That false premise is what dropped Survivance from the facade table and required a repair commit. Survivance has no well-registered station either way — its nearest is r4c2 at 55.5 m, where Azad at 23 m and Sankofa Mid at 43 m are both nearer — so its wall colour is a neighbourhood reading, flagged as provisional in campus-facades.json. (3) scripts/tmp-sample.mjs, named above as the provenance of every wall colour in this file, was never committed and does not exist in any commit. No hex here can currently be re-derived or audited. Re-measurement needs a capture rig that records camera pose per frame so footprints can be projected and the sampled patch proven to lie on the intended building.

landmarks._: Campus landmarks researched 2026-08-03 (Stuart Collection pages, press, aerials) for campus-landmarks.js. Fallen Star position was independently georeferenced - Wikipedia's coordinate is ~400 m off. Colours re-measured 2026-08-03 from 4K walk (W:fNNNN) and drone (D:fNNNN) footage; every hex below is a measurement with its frame named in the description, lifted to daylight where the drone frame was overcast or dusk.

fallenStar.cornerEvidence: D:f0034-f0036. The cottage is NOT on a corner of the main block: Jacobs Hall's south face is a comb of slender concrete stair towers, and the house sits on one of them with building mass on both sides. The georeferenced point lands 3.7 m off that south face at x=546 in local metres, west of the footprint's mid-span (504..605) - south-west, agreeing with this tag. The prose in the Fallen Star landmark entry used to say 'northeast corner' and was wrong.

landmarks.name: Sun God
landmarks.description: Niki de Saint Phalle's great bird, repainted from footage. The earlier reading had the body sprayed all over with small bright blotches, and that is wrong in the way that matters: the colour arrives as a handful of very large deliberate motifs on white. Measured D:f0100-f0101 (close aerial) and W:f0059 (eye level, sunlit): WHITE body; a scarlet head with a blue crown band and a big hooked beak a shade darker and more purple than the head itself; and behind the head a gold sunburst crest of about nine tapered spikes radiating up and out in a fan. One big concentric disc on the chest (red outer ring, blue ring, gold sun-centre) and one oval target on each outstretched wing (red, green and gold rings around a blue-red core); feet and legs painted in the same red/blue/yellow/green family. It stands on a low arch that is completely blanketed in ivy - a dark green mass with an arched opening beneath it, not the bare grey concrete assumed before; only the cap the bird stands on shows pale concrete. Bird ~4.3 m over a ~4.5 m arch. Low-poly: ivy piers + ivy lintel + pale cap, white body and wings, scarlet head, gold spike fan, and coaxial ring discs that read from either side.

landmarks.name: Fallen Star
landmarks.description: Do Ho Suh's small blue New England cottage perched at a tilt on Jacobs Hall (roof ~29 m up), cantilevered over the edge as if crash-landed. Measured D:f0034-f0036: powder-blue clapboard walls, white door/window trim, grey shingle pitched roof (lighter and bluer than the near-black the file used to carry), red brick chimney. It sits on one of the slender concrete stair towers that comb the building's SOUTH face - not on a corner of the main block, which is why it has building on both sides of it in the aerials - and hangs off that tower's south-WEST corner, with the rooftop garden (lawn, shrubs, a purple-leaf tree, ivy spilling over the tower edge) filling the rest of the tower roof inboard of the house. Low-poly: simple gabled house box ~5 m tall rotated ~10 deg off the building's grid and pitched ~10 deg over the drop. The rendered spec - position, corner, tilt, dimensions and every colour - lives in the top-level fallenStar block, not here.

landmarks.name: Snake Path
landmarks.description: Alexis Smith's 171 m long, 3 m wide winding footpath shaped like a serpent, running from Warren Mall (east end 32.881275,-117.235907) up the hillside to the Geisel Library terrace (west end 32.881024,-117.237041). Surface is hexagonal slate tiles in a scale pattern: mottled green, grey, and tan. Head (with eyes) at the top near Geisel; tail at the bottom; mid-path it coils around a small walled 'Garden of Eden' with fruit trees and passes an oversized granite book. Low-poly: a flat S-curving ribbon with green/grey checker texture, slightly raised, widening to a spade-shaped head.

landmarks.name: Silent Tree
landmarks.description: Terry Allen's dead eucalyptus tree wrapped entirely in dull grey lead sheet, standing on Library Walk just south of Geisel Library. Bare branching trunk, no leaves, matte lead grey with visible panel seams - measured W:f0151, a warm-neutral gunmetal rather than a blue steel. Classic meeting spot. Low-poly: a leafless tree of 5-8 tapering cylinders, uniform lead grey.

landmarks.name: Trees (Talking Tree)
landmarks.description: Second of Terry Allen's three lead-clad eucalyptus trunks, hidden in the living eucalyptus grove southwest of Geisel; plays spoken poems and stories from concealed speakers. Same look as Silent Tree: bare grey-lead branching trunk among tall living trees. Low-poly: identical grey leafless tree, surrounded by normal green eucalyptus.

landmarks.name: Trees (Singing Tree)
landmarks.description: Third Terry Allen lead-covered eucalyptus, ~70 m west of the Talking Tree in the same grove; emits songs. Matte grey leafless trunk with lead panel seams. Low-poly: same grey tree model reused.

landmarks.name: Bear (Warren Bear)
landmarks.description: Tim Hawkinson's teddy-bear built from eight huge rounded granite boulders (~180 tons), sitting upright in the Jacobs School engineering courtyard between CSE, EBU1, and the Bioengineering building. Warm grey-tan granite, measured twice (W:f0108 eye level, D:f0053 aerial) - a touch warmer and duller than the neutral the model was using; one giant egg boulder for the body, sphere head, four smaller boulders as arms/legs, two small ears. This is what students call the Warren Bear. Low-poly: 8-10 smooth grey spheres/ovoids stacked into a seated teddy bear.

landmarks.name: La Jolla Project (Stonehenge)
landmarks.description: Richard Fleischner's 71 blocks of pink and grey granite scattered across the Revelle College lawn south of Galbraith Hall, some stacked into post-and-lintel doorways, arches, and benches up to ~2.4 m tall — hence the 'Stonehenge' nickname. Low-poly: a dozen clusters of rectangular blocks, alternating warm pink-beige and cool grey granite, on flat green grass.

landmarks.name: Triton Statue
landmarks.description: Manuelita Brown's bronze King Triton on the plaza at the east entrance of Price Center, muscular merman rising from a wave, trident in hand, on a low stone base. Measured D:f0026 (and D:f0128 on the King Triton at the amphitheatre base, #3f4245): the patina reads dark blue-black, not brown-green. Photo spot for grads. Low-poly: dark bronze torso with raised trident, fish-tail base merging into a wave wedge, grey plinth.

landmarks.name: READ/WRITE/THINK/DREAM
landmarks.description: John Baldessari's artwork forming the main east entrance of Geisel Library: a row of tall glass doors and windows in saturated primary colors (red, blue, yellow, green panes) with the words READ, WRITE, THINK, DREAM, plus large photographic panels inside. Low-poly: the library's ground-level entry wall as a strip of vivid colored glass rectangles under the concrete tower.

landmarks.name: Geisel Library
landmarks.description: The campus icon: an 8-level brutalist 'lantern' — a concrete pedestal with four massive splayed diagonal piers holding five progressively larger-then-smaller glass floors, widest in the middle, like a spaceship or tree canopy. Raw grey concrete piers, dark tinted glass bands with narrow concrete floor slabs. Low-poly: stepped stack of square glass floors (widths ~small/large/largest/large/small) on 4 angled concrete legs.

landmarks.name: Vices and Virtues
landmarks.description: Bruce Nauman's band of 2.1 m tall neon words wrapping the top parapet of the Powell Structural Systems Laboratory (crown sits ~25 m up): seven vices superimposed on seven virtues (FAITH/LUST, HOPE/ENVY...) flashing in alternating neon colors. Measured D:f0033, which corrects two things: the host is a plain GREY board-formed concrete box, not an oxblood one, and the crown is an OPEN OXIDE-RED steel frame - an airy lattice you can see sky through, carrying the tubes and running down the building's corners as red columns. The letters are hot pink-red and mint green (daylight readings; at night they are far brighter). NOT YET RENDERED by campus-landmarks.js - the grey box belongs to campus-facades.json, and the red crown + letter band is future work. Low-poly when built: an open red steel frame band around the parapet with a glowing letter strip inside it.

landmarks.name: Two Running Violet V Forms
landmarks.description: Robert Irwin's two V-shaped runs of blue-violet plastic-coated chain-link fence held ~7.6 m in the air on slim stainless steel poles, threading between eucalyptus trunks in the grove west of Library Walk. Translucent purple-blue shimmer against the trees. Low-poly: two long thin semi-transparent violet ribbons in a shallow V plan, on skinny silver posts among eucalyptus.

landmarks.name: What Hath God Wrought
landmarks.description: Mark Bradford's 199 ft white steel pole — the tallest structure on campus — rising from Revelle College plaza, topped with a light that blinks 'What hath God wrought' in Morse code at night. Looks like an impossibly tall slender flagpole. Low-poly: a single thin white tapering cylinder with a small blinking white light cap.

landmarks.name: KAHNOP - TO TELL A STORY
landmarks.description: Ann Hamilton's ~240 m long granite walkway east of Pepper Canyon, on the route from the trolley station into campus, its pale grey stone pavers carved with raised lines of text (Kumeyaay and English words). Low-poly: a flat light-grey stone ribbon path with subtle darker text striping.

landmarks.name: Theodor Seuss Geisel Memorial (Dr. Seuss statue)
landmarks.description: Bronze of Dr. Seuss seated at his drafting desk with a 2 m Cat in the Hat standing beside him, on the terrace just west of the Geisel Library entrance. Dark brown bronze on a low grey plinth. Low-poly: seated figure at a small desk plus a tall thin cat figure with stovepipe hat, all one bronze color.

landmarks.name: Green Table
landmarks.description: Jenny Holzer's leaf-green granite picnic table and benches engraved with texts, in a grove near Peterson Hall on Ridge Walk. Low-poly: a simple picnic table, solid muted green stone.

landmarks.name: Revelle Plaza Fountain
landmarks.description: The centrepiece of Revelle Plaza, and the thing the walk aims at once it leaves Argo: a low ring basin about 8 m across with a single white aerating jet standing in the middle of it, and the tall US flagpole a dozen metres off its north side. Measured W:f0035 (and corroborated W:f0034, W:f0036): the basin is BLACK - a charcoal basalt that samples #151217 raw in the frame, which is the darkest thing on the plaza and the reason the fountain reads as a hole in the concrete rather than an ornament. The rendered #3a3437 is that reading lifted to daylight, a very dark warm charcoal rather than the literal near-black. The jet samples #a5b1b6 backlit and is rendered as lifted white foam - a single column that flares as it rises, not a fan of nozzles. Position is the surveyed OSM point 'Revelle Plaza Fountain' inside the plaza polygon both the router and the walk cross. The flagpole stand-off is parallax between W:f0034 and W:f0035, which puts it 12-17 m from the basin on the side away from the cafe umbrellas; the flag's own red/white/blue are the canonical US flag colours, NOT measurements - at this distance the flag is a handful of sky-mixed pixels. The flag itself is now built to the published US proportions - hoist 1, fly 1.9, thirteen equal stripes with seven red and red at top and bottom, union 7/13 of the hoist tall and 0.76 of the hoist wide over the top seven stripes, fifty stars in the 6/5 nine-row grid - which is a SPECIFICATION, not a measurement. So is everything else new on the pole: the 1.52 m hoist (the conventional flag for a pole this tall), the standing wave the cloth is bent onto and the direction it flies, the gold ball finial and truck (flagGold), the halyard (halyard) and the cleat (cleat). What a source actually settles is only that the pole is there and that it flies the US flag - Revelle College's own page lists 'the May 1970 Peace Memorial and the U.S. Flag' as what the Plaza hosts (revelle.ucsd.edu/events), and W:f0034-f0036 place it. No frame on this campus resolves the hardware at 15 m. Low-poly: charcoal rim cylinder, dark water disc, one flaring foam cone, tapered white pole with ball finial, halyard and cleat, and a thirteen-stripe flag welded into four instanced ribbons.

landmarks.name: Pergola Swings (Ridge Walk at Muir Field)
landmarks.description: One of a pair of identical rest stations the walk passes: a long black steel post-and-beam trellis with a flat roof of pale timber slats, three hanging bench swings on rods under it and fixed grey benches alongside. Measured W:f0013-f0014, where the run stands at the edge of the mown Muir field with the walk on its other side. Every reading in those frames is against the sun, so the steel samples #0c090a to #2f3036 and the slats read as silhouette: the frame black #3a3634 and the lit timber #c9c2b2 are the daylight values, and the benches #8a8378 with them. Placed on the east side of Ridge Walk at the field's edge, beside the route between Muir and Peterson. Low-poly: two rows of posts, two beams, a rack of slats, three swing seats on rods, two fixed benches.

landmarks.name: Pergola Swings (Revelle Walk)
landmarks.description: The second station of the same furniture family, on the Revelle stretch of the walk north of Bonner Hall. Measured W:f0026 (seen up the walk) and W:f0027 (standing in it, a swing seat hanging on its rods a metre from the lens). Same black steel frame, same pale slat roof, same grey benches as the Muir station - which is the point: it is a repeat, and repeats are what make a campus legible. It sits in the planted median between the bike lane and the pedestrian walk, so the route passes within a few metres of it. The colours are the Muir station's daylight values; both frames here are backlit too.

landmarks.name: Mayer/Bonner Folded-Plate Canopy
landmarks.description: The Revelle silhouette, and the one piece of building shape on this walk that a flat wall cannot fake: a continuous eave of literal triangular concrete prisms - a folded plate - running the length of the Mayer and Bonner arcade on slender round columns, cream #d8d4c6. Measured W:f0022-f0023, where the prisms are the whole top-right of the frame; both readings are of the shaded underside (#4a4a3b, #585351) so the cream is the daylight value. The line it runs along is not stored here: the builder takes the WEST edge of each host's own footprint out of campus-3d.json, so the canopy stays welded to the buildings if the massing ever moves. The two hosts present one unbroken west face about 160 m long, which is the whole east side of the Revelle stretch the route walks. Low-poly: one instanced prism per 2.4 m of run with a column every 4.8 m.

landmarks.name: Sun God Lawn reference - Untitled (Asher fountain)
landmarks.description: Michael Asher's granite drinking fountain shaped like a commercial office fountain, oddly alone on the plaza north of Price Center. Speckled grey granite box. Low-poly: a knee-high grey rectangular block with a basin notch.

measured.heightNote: The 2014 drawn surface is FLAT at 23.5-23.9 m under the whole footprint and across the north apron (sampled on a 2 m grid against makeSurfaceSampler), so there is no storey-high step between the north plaza and the ground at the building's south edge, and the survey's earlier reading — LiDAR 16.6 above the lawn, ArcGIS 12.8 above a plaza one storey higher — cannot be what these two numbers are. That flat pad is LOCAL: the same sampler puts a ~26.8 m ridge 8-9 m west of the ring (west.gradeNote), 27.1 m within 25 m to the south (the lawn climbs past z ~503) and ~26.8 m under the east tree band, which is why every ground field in this section is draped over the drawn terrain and every solid seated per-item on it, never hung on a 23.6 level line. On the flat pad the ring stands on, LiDAR 16.6 is simply the roof above grade on all four sides, and this section puts its eaves exactly there, on top of the measured mass, so nothing measured is left standing above the roof. How the 16.6 divides is read off oceanlight-21220.jpg, which is near-orthographic: scaling that elevation so grade-to-roof is 16.6 gives a 5.6 m lower glazed band, a 3.2 m terrace zone, a 4.5 m upper glazed band and a 3.2 m roof edge — two levels of about 7.4 m and a slab of about 1.8, which sums back to 16.6 with no residual. Two glazed bands split by one mid-level balcony is what the north, south and west photographs all show, and a 7.4 m level is corroborated on the north by ad01-entry-before.jpg, where the plaza-level glazing stands about three door-heights tall. LiDAR decides the ground and the top; the photographs decide only how the space between them divides.
measured.conflict: PARTLY RESOLVED by the repo orthophoto (2026): a raised ~29 m central block with a 9x9 skylight grid demonstrably exists, so the 3.8 m ArcGIS/LiDAR delta has a physical owner — 12.8 is plausibly the low deck and 16.6 the highest return over the block or the penthouses. What stays unresolved is HOW HIGH the block stands (no shadow is measurable; its rim reveal is symmetric on all four sides) and which roof object owns the 16.6 maximum. The drawn measured mass extrudes the whole footprint to 16.6, so this section expresses the roofscape as curb-scale relief on that top rather than re-deriving the facade datum — see roof.datumNote. ArcGIS's 3 levels vs 2 expressed elevations is still taken as an internal third level, unbuilt.

grid.datumNote: standoff, roofOut and every facade projection are measured from the GLAZING PLANE, not from the measured ring: 3.4 m is what the photographs read between the glass and the strut line, and it has to stay 3.4 m however far out the glazing itself has to hang to clear the drawn mass.
grid.calibration: The architect's plan gives 10.83 m between pair centres. That number was calibrated against a 45.8 m enclosed block, and it does NOT survive contact with the surveyed 62 m footprint: the measured ring is the wall this section is allowed to hang on, and five pairs at 10.83 m only span 45.8 m of it. So the drawing's SPACING is dropped and its COUNT is kept — five pairs, 2.45 m inside a pair, both of which are independently countable in oceanlight-21220.jpg — spread across the measured face. The measured world decides scale; the photographs decide what is on it.
grid.moduleNote: The coffer module survives that, because it is corroborated twice over: it is the drawing's own pair spacing over eight (10.83 / 8 = 1.354), and it is also the size that puts the 46 coffers counted across the elevation onto the 62 m measured face (62.0 / 46 = 1.348). The two agree to 6 mm. The oversail is six of them, counted in ad01-entry-before.jpg and again in wm-from-below.jpg.
grid.source: ad-plan-L2.jpg, Kevin deFreitas Architects Second Floor Plan, 02.17.12

column.profileNote: Half-widths are the LATHE CIRCUMRADIUS of a four-sided section, so what an elevation actually shows is radius x sqrt(2): a 0.83 head reads as the photographed 1.17 m bracket and the 0.38 waist as a 0.54 m shaft. Not a straight box and not a plain taper: thin at the waist, sweeping out below into a wide flat foot and flaring above into a broad bracket that meets the beam hard. Section is square with the diagonal facing the wall, which is what ad01 and ucsdmap both show.

roofEdge.source: crop-roofedge.jpg (2011) and wm-from-below.jpg (2026) — present in both epochs

facade.wallStandoffNote: Not a style choice. campus-massing.js extrudes the UNIVERSITY'S massing ring, which stands up to 0.799 m outside the OSM ring this section is anchored to. Glazing hung any closer than that disappears inside the drawn box on the east elevation. The standoff is that clearance plus 0.15 m and nothing more.
facade.mullionNote: ESTIMATE, 1.5-1.8 m read off ad01; finer than the coffer module, never equal to it.

entry.beamNote: The two beams ride the middle pair's column lines and carry the 'Galbraith Hall' lettering on their outer fascia. The lettering itself is ABSENT: there is no text mechanism in this renderer and a painted-on rectangle would be worse than nothing.
entry.signNote: The 'Theatre & Dance Department' hanging blade, in both wm-from-below and flickr.

west.gradeNote: The 2014 ground rises 3.2 m from x -8 to a ridge at x -16.5 that runs dead straight for the whole length of the west face. That ridge is what the lava wall in ucsdmap.jpg retains, but it is also exactly the shape a bare-earth classifier leaves along a hedge or a wall line, so nothing here asserts it is topography: the wall is placed at its crest, OUTSIDE the roof, and every solid on this side is seated per-item on the drawn surface rather than on a level.

absent: The true heights of everything on the roof — the raised skylight block ([estimated] 1.5-2.5 m), the three penthouses and the six mech enclosures. The orthophoto is nadir and its rim reveal casts no measurable shadow; LiDAR stores one maximum per building. Plan positions are sourced; every height up there is expression-only (roof.datumNote).
The interior barrel-vault ceiling geometry (ad-2012-194.jpg) and how it meets the 9x9 skylight grid above it — interior, unbuilt.
The east ground beyond x ~90 — active construction in the current orthophoto epoch. Disturbed earth, plant and a temporary haul road are in flux and stay unbuilt.
The low wall or step running diagonally along the SE lawn's north edge, and the lawn's shrub masses — visible as smudges in the orthophoto, never resolved to a geometry.
Bike racks, light poles, bollards and wayfinding signage anywhere around the building — visible as smudges in ucsdmap.jpg, never resolved.
The dark collar at some column bases in ucsdmap.jpg — unresolved between paint, shadow and a leaning object.
The 'Galbraith Hall' and 'Theatre & Dance Department' lettering. The blades that carry it are built; the glyphs are not, because this renderer has no text mechanism.
The pre-2013 CLICS teal sign (#61838d, gold lettering) — a dead epoch, superseded by the red entry canopy.
The green metal picnic table and the coral tree east of the west court in ucsdmap.jpg — too coarse in the only frame that holds them.
The La Jolla Project granite blocks on the south lawn — already built by campus-landmarks.json, and never duplicated here.
Interior fitout of every level, including the 417-seat lecture hall the plan sheets describe.
The NW solid stair/service piers in grey exposed aggregate (ucsdmap.jpg, west inventory) — one oblique frame with no measurable plan position or count; named, not built.

The recessed can lights under the two entry beams (ad01-entry-before.jpg) — the cylindrical colonnade downlights are built; the in-beam cans are too small in the one frame that shows them to place on the beam.

roof.source: sat_galbraith.png — crop of the repo's own Google orthophoto chunk_4_7.jpg (docs/data/textures, source: google, generated 2026-08-04, 0.125 m/px, world mapping in textures/manifest.json). Positions read off it are +-0.5 m. Per CLAUDE.md satellite imagery is a build-time measurement source only.
roof.datumNote: NO DOUBLE-COUNTING of the 3.8 m. LiDAR 16.6 is a MAXIMUM return, and campus-massing.js draws the measured box to that height over the WHOLE footprint — so the visible box top already stands at the highest real point of this roof. The real low deck sits [estimated] 1.5-2.5 m below it and is buried inside the drawn mass; nothing can be drawn under the box top. Everything here therefore seats ON the drawn box top (the structure it stands on) and rises only curb-scale above it: skylight curbs 0.18 m, block rim 0.12 m, penthouse/mech expression 0.28-0.35 m. Plan positions and pitches are SOURCED; the expression heights are [estimated] and deliberately suppressed so nothing stands a storey above the LiDAR maximum.

block.heightNote: [estimated] 1.5-2.5 m above the true low deck (inventory + the 2012 interior photo); 2.0 m carried as the declared middle. NOT drawn as 2 m of box — see datumNote.
block.revealNote: A dark reveal/gutter 0.5-1.0 m wide rings the block on all four sides in the orthophoto; symmetric, so it is a reveal and not a cast shadow.

skylights.pitchNote: The orthophoto measures a 2.75 m pitch (sigma ~0.05 m); 2 coffer modules is 2.708 m. They agree to under 5 cm per bay, and this building solves on one grid or it is wrong, so the pitch is DERIVED as 2 x grid.module and the raw measurement is recorded here. Field centred on the sourced block rectangle (its centre sits 0.8 m west and 3.6 m north of the ring centroid — the block itself is not quite central and the field follows it). The squares read WHITE from above: white-capped curbs, not dark glass.

roof.penthouseNote: Two stair/lift penthouses projecting north from the block and one large one projecting south; the south one wears a pale seamed metal roof in the orthophoto. z0 433.0 < the ring's 428.9 + 4, i.e. the north pair sit just inside the north edge. Expression height 0.35 m [estimated] — see datumNote.
roof.mechNote: Six dark-walled service enclosures with pale equipment inside, on the low deck. Expression height 0.28 m walls + 0.34 m equipment [estimated] — see datumNote.

east.source: sat_east_ground.png — repo Google orthophoto (chunk_4_7 + chunk_5_7, source: google, generated 2026-08-04), world x 40..110, z 420..505. The building's east edge measures x ~54.7 against the ring's 54.6.
east.recessNote: ~2.2 m of permanently shaded ground under the roof oversail, full length.
east.walkNote: ~3.1 m pale tan unit-paver / scored-concrete walk running the full north-south length; a fine banded texture is visible. Band pitch 0.45 m [estimated] off the visible banding.
east.footPadNote: A row of pale ~1.0-1.4 m squares along the building side of the walk at ~11-12 m spacing, read as the colonnade column feet showing past the roof edge. Pads are drawn under the BUILT east strut pairs (derived pairSpacing 14.19 m), because pads not under their own columns would be worse than none. TENSION, recorded not resolved: the orthophoto's 11-12 m square spacing sits closer to the drawing's dropped 10.83 m than to the derived 14.19 m; at 0.125 m/px with ~1.2 m blobs neither is excluded.
east.dgNote: Broad decomposed-granite band under the mature tree canopies out to x~89; the trees themselves stay the measured tree layer's business. Split into two rects because York Hall's measured footprint reaches x 83.9 / z 431.8 at its south-west corner and nothing invented may lie inside a measured building.
east.lawnNote: South-east lawn patch; its shrub masses and the low diagonal wall/step stay absent.
east.constructionNote: EPOCH LIMIT: beyond x ~90 the orthophoto shows active construction — disturbed earth, plant, a temporary haul road, a large white-roofed structure. That ground is in flux and is left UNBUILT.

plaza.label: Revelle Plaza landscape — trees, ground features and furniture of Zone 1 (the ground between Keeling, York, Argo, Blake and Galbraith)
plaza.epoch: Photographs 2006-2026 decide what exists and how it looks; the georeferenced satellite plan (Google chunks, fetched 2026-08-03) decides plan positions; LiDAR 2014 decides every re-skinned trunk's position, height and crown radius. The coral tree post-dates the LiDAR (planted Feb 2014) and is the one tree here with no measured trunk.
plaza.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Everything here is modelled off dated photographs and the plan-only satellite read in scratchpad/research/zone1-plaza-landscape.md. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. The treeOverrides re-skin measured LiDAR trunks by position key: heights and crown radii are copied VERBATIM from docs/data/campus-lidar.json (whose r is clamped at 7.5 m and h at 30 m — floors, not measurements). No colour here is sampled from raw satellite pixels. NO PALMS: twelve palm taxa are on the campus list and zero appear in any Zone 1 photograph, so none are built.

treeOverrides.note: Position-keyed re-skins of measured LiDAR trunks (key = 'x,z' exactly as in docs/data/campus-lidar.json trees). This module builds the ultra models; MAIN MUST SKIP the default blob rendering for every key in skipMeasuredKeys or each tree draws twice. Species verdicts are photo-sourced (zone1-plaza-landscape.md §1): the York belt is Torrey pine (the h>=16 heuristic mislabels it eucalyptus), the plaza/Argo broadleafs are ficus, eucalyptus only east of York and on the Keeling west road. Groups E-north and G stay generic blobs — per-tree confidence is too low to re-skin them.

pines.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011); Pinus torreyana on the official campus species list. Clear bole 55-65% of height, open irregular candelabra crown reading ~40-50% sky.

ficus.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) — pale sinuous multi-stem trunks under tight dark canopies; Ficus microcarpa/retusa/rubiginosa all on the official list. Plaza-core group C plus the two small trees hard against Argo's south side.

eucalyptus.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the grove edge east of York (group B), plus the tall road-frontage trees on the Keeling west road (group F, h>=14; keeling-inventory.md corroborates).

coral.source: today.ucsd.edu/news_uploads/memorial1.jpg (Feb 2014) — multi-stem, smooth pale grey-green bark, sparse open branching, planted in a ~2.5 m bare-earth ring for the memorial unveiling. NOT in the 2014 LiDAR (planted at/after that epoch).
coral.tag: [estimated] size — a 5 m nursery specimen in 2014 grown to a 12-year irrigated coral tree; species unresolved among three Erythrina on the campus list, so it is generic and unflowered

fountain.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012 aerial) + satellite plan + Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) + Galbraith Hall with Revelle Fountain (2024). Low square plinth with a circular basin recessed into its top deck; running in 2024. Centre is the landmark's surveyed OSM point (position from OSM wins over the photo/satellite read).
fountain.replacesNote: MAIN MUST SUPPRESS the landmark ring-fountain basin + jet (campus-landmarks 'Revelle Plaza Fountain') when this section is present, exactly as skipMeasuredKeys suppresses the blob trees — its builder draws an 8 m basin and jet at this same surveyed point, so without suppression two fountains interpenetrate. KEEP the landmark's flagpole, flag and hardware: they are that entry's, not this section's.

memorial.source: today.ucsd.edu memorial1.jpg + memorial2.jpg (Feb 2014). Half-disc concrete slab FLUSH in the lawn, brick soldier trim on the straight edge, ~15 flush light lenses in a star figure with engraved connecting lines, curved concrete bench on a lava-rock rubble base.
memorial.lensNote: [estimated] layout — a star figure of ~15 lenses radiating from an off-centre node, as memorial1.jpg shows; the exact chart is not resolvable in either frame

lawns.source: satellite plan at 8 px/m — two panels split by a paved cross-walk, correcting part 1's single 60x30 field. Lawn colour reused from the Keeling agent's independent read.

arcs.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) mid-ground — at every band crossing the panel corners are struck with a 1.5-2.0 m radius and the brick coursing FANS to follow each arc. Derived per-crossing from the revelle section's own paving cells; pitch/band/radius are the repo's ground-truthed values.

dgBelt.source: satellite plan — bare tan ground under the York-belt Torrey pines; decomposed granite is confirmed on the north approach behind the lava walls
dgBelt.tag: [estimated] extent — the belt's edges are read off the satellite plan, its surface off the north-approach photographs

lamp.source: Revelle_Plaza__UCSD.JPG (2011), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011), Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) — three frames agree; scaled off the published 54-inch banner. Pole 5.5-6.0 m built at 5.75; section built square 0.12 (round-vs-square unresolved at plaza distance). Crossarm pair of 20x54-inch banners, bottom bracket 2.8-3.1 m, top 4.2-4.5 m; gold-dominant design. The photographed pair contradicts the newer one-banner brand rule — epoch conflict, photos win for this model.

benches.source: Revelle_Plaza__UCSD.JPG (2011) — a near-continuous type-A row along the plaza/lawn boundary facing the plaza, broken where a lamppost lands; singles in front of the north-approach lava walls facing the plaza

binPairs.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) square precast bin + the aerial's cylindrical bins standing in pairs at the lawn edge

bikes.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) — 25+ bicycles double-parked on the Argo rack run; at plaza distance the bikes are the object, so the bikes are built over the existing rack row

terraces.source: satellite plan (2026 imagery — current epoch) — two cafe terraces with ~2.5 m round umbrellas: 4-5 blue at the plaza north-east, a larger mixed blue/orange terrace at Revelle Commons / 64 Degrees

absent: Palms — twelve taxa on the campus list, zero in any Zone 1 photograph. Not present, not built.
Jacarandas — present on campus, no evidence inside Zone 1. Not added to make the plaza prettier.
The salmon/copper lawn tree (~x 5-15, z 385-395) — candidate Koelreuteria bipinnata, unconfirmed and possibly not surviving to 2026; a wrong salmon tree mid-lawn is a very visible error.
The coral tree's Erythrina species and its flowers — three candidates on the campus list, the leafed-out photo cannot settle it; built generic and unflowered.
Drinking fountains — one ambiguous ~1.0 m object that is equally likely a bollard. Ladder exhausted.
The memorial's 'marble plaque' — whether it is the inscribed slab itself or a separate element is unresolved in both photographs.
The memorial's chiselled inscription lettering — the curved line of hand-cut capitals is real but below geometry resolution here.
El Mac's mural 'An Enduring Spell' on Argo — still no photograph. Not invented.
The north-west terrace steps — riser/tread never resolved in any frame.
Curbs and ramps — not resolved anywhere in the zone.

The flagpole — built and kept by the campus-landmarks 'Revelle Plaza Fountain' entry, not this section. The inventory's §3i correction (both the 2006 photo and the ~2012 aerial put it in or at the edge of the lawn on a small concrete pad, not out in the open paving, and 18-22 m tall not 15) is DECLARED here but not applied — campus-landmarks is outside this section's scope. Its finial, halyard and cleat remain specification, not measurement.

The wayfinding blade sign (§3f, measured in Argo_Hall.jpg — ~0.35 x 0.9 m panel on a post, top ~2.2 m) — its dims are measured but no source resolves its plan position; better absent than guessed onto the paving.

The two free-standing information-panel types (§3f, measured in Revelle_Plaza_Path__UCSD.jpg — a ~0.5 x 0.7 m board on a slim post, and a larger ~0.9 x 1.3 m directory on legs) — dims measured, plan positions unresolved; left unbuilt.

The yellow-topped Argo-side bulletin kiosk (§3d, Argo_Hall.jpg — ~x -50, z 400) — its position is inferred from the building's framing, not measured in plan, and the revelle section's gold-top kiosk at (48, 340) is the plaza NE one, not this. Left unbuilt rather than placed on an inference.
The Galbraith frontage planting-bed band (z 415-423) — real, but it belongs to the Galbraith/Revelle building passes, not this ground module.
Group E-north and Group G trees — per-tree species confidence too low to re-skin; they keep the measured blob rendering.
Bench type B (wood-topped) near Mayer — part 1's find, not re-verified; left to the revelle section.
Lamppost section round vs square — invisible at plaza distance; built square 0.12 m.
